races.name: Queen Mary Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies)

runners_data.name: Alta Regina
runners_data.note: Won sole start over 5f on Good ground; James McDonald in the saddle is a major plus, and while she is a natural prominent racer who has been mapped to midfield due to overcrowding forward, her tactical ability to slot anywhere makes her dangerous regardless of position.

runners_data.name: Armor Supreme
runners_data.note: Two runs both over 5f Good, winning latest — Rossa Ryan booking suggests confidence, and though her preference is to race prominently, the congested nature of this draw means she may have to settle slightly wider than ideal.

runners_data.name: Big Negotiator
runners_data.note: Progressive form string of 3-2-1 over 5f on Good, all three runs on similar ground; P J McDonald ensures she is professionally placed, and she is a natural prominent runner who shapes as a genuine each-way contender if she can find her spot in the early stages.

runners_data.name: Bint Archange
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 5f on Good ground with a runner-up on similar; Richard Hughes trains this filly with encouraging juvenile form, and though she wants to race prominently, she has the form to cope if briefly shuffled back in a messy break.

runners_data.name: Celtic Dispute
runners_data.note: Won on Firm ground over 5f and is bred for quick surfaces; Soumillon is an astute big-field jockey, though she carries a headgear entry (blinkers) and her sole run came on Firm rather than Good to Firm which introduces a marginal going query.

runners_data.name: Crownbreaker
runners_data.note: Twice placed over 5f on Good — both a second and third — without winning; lightly raced with UNKNOWN style, and David Egan will need to find a clear path in a 28-runner dash where unbeaten fillies dominate the market.

runners_data.name: Crystal Queen
runners_data.note: Back-to-back form of 2-1 over 5f on Good gives her solid platform; Colin Keane is a high-calibre jockey for Fahey, and though overcrowding means she will be shuffled from her natural prominent position, she has the ability to overcome a slightly deeper draw.

runners_data.name: Drazinda
runners_data.note: Won sole run over 5f on Heavy ground — the significant going concern here is that Good to Firm at Ascot is markedly quicker than her only experience; Barzalona is a fine pilot but this filly is mapped to the rear through redistribution, racing well outside her comfort zone both stylistically and underfoot.

runners_data.name: Envision
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 5f Good after a fourth first time out; wears blinkers, races prominently by nature but is shown in midfield through redistribution, and Silvestre De Sousa will need a fortunate run through a congested field to maximise her.

runners_data.name: Fast Track
runners_data.note: Two runs, both placing without winning on Good ground; natural prominent racer squeezed to midfield on the map through overcrowding, and without a win to her name yet Rob Hornby will be under pressure to deliver a first success at Group 2 level on a big-field track.

runners_data.name: Havana Lightning
runners_data.note: Won last time over 5f Good after a fifth — showed resilience; Billy Loughnane is an in-form lightweight jockey, and despite her natural prominent style being mapped back by redistribution, she has the profile of a filly who can handle traffic if her recent win is taken at face value.

runners_data.name: Kentucky Rain
runners_data.note: Only run produced a second over 5f Good — lightly raced with no style confirmation; Cieren Fallon's booking is noted but this filly's redistribution to hold-up suggests she cannot be relied upon to settle in an unfamiliar deep position in a 28-runner field.

runners_data.name: Love A Giggle
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins over 5f including on Standard ground show consistency; Clifford Lee stable companion to Wild Blossom under Burke, and though she is a genuinely prominent type mapped to the rear because of field imbalance, her unbeaten record lends her claims even from an awkward drawn berth.

runners_data.name: Lover Girl
runners_data.note: Three runs with two wins and a third, all over 5f — the most experienced of the prominent types; Rowan Scott has Group race experience and the filly's natural prominent profile is one she should be able to execute with a 28-runner field spreading across the track.

runners_data.name: Magic Effort
runners_data.note: Won over 5f Good on debut before a fourth; Ismail Mohammed is a solid juvenile handler and this filly has genuine each-way claims if she can reproduce her winning effort — her style sits naturally in the prominent zone without redistribution.

runners_data.name: Miss Lizzy
runners_data.note: Career form shows a win over 6f on Standard but struggles on Good ground (two finishes of 4th and 7th at the trip); wears a tongue-tie and Charlie Fellowes will hope a clear run in a big field softens any going reservation, but course form suggests caution.

runners_data.name: More Champagne
runners_data.note: US-trained by Thomas Morley, sole run was a win, going classified UNKNOWN — the most opaque entry in the race; John Velazquez brings elite pedigree to the saddle and if this filly translates American speed to Good to Firm turf she is a major wildcard.

runners_data.name: Niewiadoma
runners_data.note: One win over 5f Good followed by a ninth — wide swings in form are a concern; Luke Morris will need to position carefully in midfield, and the drop in form last time out clouds whether the winning effort was a true benchmark.

runners_data.name: Pershaada
runners_data.note: Won most recently over 5f Good after a third and second — progressive filly in form; Richard Hannon has the best T14 strike rate among the prominent trainers here with 9/44, and Sean Levey knows his horses well enough to navigate a 28-runner field from a prominent pitch.

runners_data.name: Princesse d'Orange
runners_data.note: Three runs including a win on Soft ground but both Good-ground outings produced a 3rd and 5th — the going concern on Good to Firm is genuine; Daniel Tudhope can help her overcome it but her record strongly skews towards easier ground.

runners_data.name: Ruiva
runners_data.note: Single win with UNKNOWN going classification — Wesley Ward's second string here; Juan Hernandez brings American track experience and if the filly's raw speed translates to Ascot's quick turf this could be a dangerous outsider, but the preparation and style are entirely unknown quantities.

runners_data.name: Senorita Bonita
runners_data.note: Won her only start over 5f Good in stylish fashion; William Buick and the Crisford yard are a formidable combination in big-field sprints, and with no redistribution flag she is one of the fillies most likely to actually secure her natural prominent position from the off.

runners_data.name: Shimmering Sun
runners_data.note: Won sole run over 5f Good — consistent with a clean profile; Dylan Browne McMonagle has risen sharply in profile and this filly for Harry Eustace carries unexplored upside, racing from a natural prominent position without style compromise.

runners_data.name: Shining Moment
runners_data.note: Ward's first string alongside Ruiva — won second start over 5f with UNKNOWN going, wears blinkers; Oisin Murphy is unquestionably the key upgrade here, and if Ward's American speed converts to Ascot fast ground, this filly is the most dangerous unknown in the field.

runners_data.name: Velozee
runners_data.note: Two wins over 5f including on Soft, with a fourth over 6f Good — the distance and going sit squarely in her range; W J Lee for Twomey is a trainer who targets these big juvenile sprints, and her form profile is consistent and honest.

runners_data.name: Victorious
runners_data.note: The only runner here with two wins over 6f on Good — Ryan Moore and Aidan O'Brien is the most powerful combination in the race; stepping back to 5f is a minor query but the horse's tactical speed and class suggest she will push forward hard and be very difficult to pass.

runners_data.name: Wild Blossom
runners_data.note: Won sole run over 5f Good — Burke's second juvenile here alongside Love A Giggle; James Doyle will settle her patiently though her natural midfield style means she is redistributed to the rear, racing somewhat out of profile in this pace-heavy field.

runners_data.name: Your Song
runners_data.note: Confirmed non-runner — their withdrawal removes the only genuine lone front-runner; their absence means no horse can dictate uncontested, and the race pace is now likely to be sharper and more competitive as several prominent types contest the lead.

races.paceDynamic: With Your Song confirmed as a non-runner, this 28-runner Group 2 sprint loses its lone acknowledged front-runner, meaning the early lead will be contested among several natural prominent-racing types who all want to be on or near the pace. Senorita Bonita, Victorious, Lover Girl, and Pershaada all carry prominent profiles and are likely to push forward from the gates, creating a genuinely contested early pace over Ascot's straight five furlongs on Good to Firm ground. That competitive early tempo should ensure the race is run at a true gallop throughout, compressing the advantage for any horse trying to steal a march and keeping the race honest enough that finishing power becomes decisive. This race shape firmly favours horses with a prominent-to-midfield profile who can travel smoothly within the first wave, because true hold-up types in this field are largely redistributed prominent racers — their natural position is forward, not back — meaning closers who need a genuine pace collapse to pounce are racing against their own instincts. The field holds considerably more prominent and front-running types than the race can accommodate; Senorita Bonita, Victorious, Lover Girl, and Crystal Queen are best-placed to actually secure their preferred berth given draw, jockey quality, and recent winning form.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Prominent Types Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If the early pace is genuinely contested and Senorita Bonita, Victorious, or Lover Girl secure cover just off the leaders without burning fuel, allowing them to quicken decisively in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: If the early pace is genuinely contested and Senorita Bonita, Victorious, or Lover Girl secure cover just off the leaders without burning fuel, allowing them to quicken decisively in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Pace Collapses Midfield
scenarios.trigger: If the multiple prominent types fail to coordinate, the pace fragments and a horse tracking just off a false rhythm delivers the decisive late surge.
scenarios.body: If the multiple prominent types fail to coordinate, the pace fragments and a horse tracking just off a false rhythm delivers the decisive late surge.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Drawn Wide Flier Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If a wide-drawn prominent type avoids the early congestion on the near side and benefits from cleaner air and better ground out wide, powering home late.
scenarios.body: If a wide-drawn prominent type avoids the early congestion on the near side and benefits from cleaner air and better ground out wide, powering home late.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Outsider Exploits Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If early crowding, stumbles, or wide-field interference causes disruption to the fancied prominent runners and a lightly-raced or unknown quantity produces a career-best effort.
scenarios.body: If early crowding, stumbles, or wide-field interference causes disruption to the fancied prominent runners and a lightly-raced or unknown quantity produces a career-best effort.

watchPoints.text: Victorious carries the strongest combination of class, jockey (Moore), and trainer (O'Brien) in the race and is likely to push forward aggressively — watch whether she can actually secure a prominent pitch before the race develops; if she does, she is the primary threat.

The 28-runner field creates significant early congestion risk — watch the first furlong for bumping or shuffling that could compromise several of the redistributed prominent types (Alta Regina, Armor Supreme, Crystal Queen) whose true style is forward but who cannot all get there.

races.name: Queen's Vase (Group 2)

runners_data.name: Asakir
runners_data.note: Placed at Grade-level in Ireland on soft and good ground, his natural game is to race prominently but this field has too many similar types ahead of him, meaning he is likely to find himself further back than ideal and racing against his instincts.|

runners_data.name: Del Maro
runners_data.note: Godolphin's representative has excellent Good-ground form (six of seven starts on that surface), Buick in the saddle, and the profile of a horse who settles handily and picks up — the step to 1m6f looks within range for a lightly-framed improver.|

runners_data.name: Galiyan
runners_data.note: Rated highest in the field alongside Point Of Law at OR 120, Balding's colt won his last two including over 1m4f at Goodwood on Good; the return to a longer trip and a sound surface suits, and Murphy is the booking.|

runners_data.name: Limestone
runners_data.note: Three consecutive wins including two on Good ground, the most recent over 1m5f — O'Brien's three-year-old arrives in peak form and the extra distance looks well within his compass, making him one of the most straightforward profiles in the race.|

runners_data.name: Magnetude
runners_data.note: James Owen's gelding is a dual winner on Good ground over 1m4f-1m5f but is a natural front-runner who will find the traffic busier than he would like here; his chance hinges on finding a prominent berth against classier and better-rated rivals.|

runners_data.name: Mr Colonel
runners_data.note: Keane rides for Fahey, and this horse has placed four times in five starts on Good ground — durable and consistent, he travels well enough but may lack the decisive acceleration of the top-rated horses in a quality-test finish.|

runners_data.name: Point Of Law
runners_data.note: Gosden-trained, Doyle-ridden, and the race's sole genuine front-runner — his two Good-ground runs have both been to a high level (including a Listed win over 1m2f) and the question is whether 1m6f stretches his stamina sufficiently to hold on.|

runners_data.name: Port Of Spain
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore takes the ride for Aidan O'Brien but this horse's form reads as patchy — one win from seven, and his last five outings include a fifth at this course; his hold-up style needs a pace that may not materialise.|

runners_data.name: Ranga Tang
runners_data.note: The second James Owen runner in the race, a winner on Good ground over 1m4f at Nottingham; like stablemate Magnetude he is a natural pace-angle horse who may be outmanoeuvred for position by classier, better-rated rivals earlier in the race.|

runners_data.name: Ravenspire
runners_data.note: K R Burke's unbeaten two-from-two, both victories on Good ground over 1m4f — the run-style makes him a compelling each-way profile if he can work into a prominent position, but the 53-day absence and big class rise are legitimate query marks.|

runners_data.name: Wareeth
runners_data.note: Archie Watson's horse has won twice including on Good/Standard and carries headgear; a natural pace-angle type who is shown at the rear of the map due to field congestion — Marquand will need to be positive from the outset to avoid being further detached than his form warrants.|

races.paceDynamic: Point Of Law is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 11-runner field and, crucially, faces no genuine pace pressure — with all other prominent types redistributed or unlikely to aggressively contest the early lead, he can dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop over this extended 1m6f trip on Good to Firm ground. Del Maro, Galiyan, and Limestone are the prominent horses best positioned to track him in the first two or three slots, with Asakir, Ravenspire, Ranga Tang, Magnetude, and Wareeth all natural front-to-prominent types who cannot all achieve their preferred position and will be shuffled back further than ideal. The result is a race likely to be run at a measured, honest tempo — not a dawdle but not a true test of stamina either — which compresses the field and sets up a contest that will be decided by quality and acceleration in the final two furlongs rather than a gruelling war of attrition. This shape strongly favours horses who can travel prominently with minimal fuss and quicken off a sound but unspectacular gallop — Galiyan (highest OR, Andrew Balding) and Limestone (in cracking form, three consecutive wins) are archetypal beneficiaries of this profile, while genuine hold-up horses face a reduced target to aim at.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Tempo, Quality Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Point Of Law dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race becomes a quality test in the straight.
scenarios.body: If Point Of Law dictates an uncontested, moderate gallop and the race becomes a quality test in the straight.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Drifts, Stayers Grind
scenarios.trigger: If Point Of Law slows the race to a near-crawl and late stamina becomes the determining factor over the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: If Point Of Law slows the race to a near-crawl and late stamina becomes the determining factor over the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Battles Out
scenarios.trigger: If one or two of the redistributed prominent types force their way to the front early and inject unexpected urgency into the pace.
scenarios.body: If one or two of the redistributed prominent types force their way to the front early and inject unexpected urgency into the pace.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop From Rear
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is fast enough to set up the race for hold-up horses arriving from off the bridle in the final quarter-mile.
scenarios.body: If the pace is fast enough to set up the race for hold-up horses arriving from off the bridle in the final quarter-mile.

watchPoints.text: Point Of Law (Gosden/Doyle) is the race's only genuine pace-setter — watch whether he allows himself to be headed or pressed in the first half-mile, as any challenge to his lead would transform this from a controlled test into a significantly stronger-run affair.

Ravenspire (Burke/Lee) is unbeaten in two but has been off 53 days and faces a sharp class jump to Group 2 — if he breaks sharply and forces his way to the front alongside Point Of Law, the tempo lifts and the scenario changes materially.

Monitor the early positions of Asakir, Magnetude, and Ranga Tang — all are natural prominent types who cannot all get their preferred spot, and any jostling or wide runs for position in the first furlong could elevate the early pace unexpectedly.

Galiyan's stamina over 1m6f is lightly tested (only two career starts), and while both were on Good ground, Andrew Balding will have prepared him specifically for this trip — watch his position turning out of the back straight as an indicator of whether Murphy is confident in his staying power.

Port Of Spain (Moore/A P O'Brien) has shown a tendency to race in rear and his recent form over 8-10f has been underwhelming — in a race that may not be strongly run, Ryan Moore may look to slot closer than usual, which is worth tracking from the stalls.

races.name: Duke Of Cambridge Stakes (Group 2) (Fillies & Mares)

runners_data.name: Jancis
runners_data.note: Five-year-old who handles good ground well (10 from 11 in similar conditions), sits naturally prominent and with Sean Levey rides a horse capable of quick, clean racing from the front rank; headgear noted (hg:t) and 24 days since last run is fine — straightforward prep.

runners_data.name: Arisaig
runners_data.note: Charlie Johnston's runner comes here off a 46-day break with solid recent form at this trip, but despite being a natural prominent racer she is one of several such types that cannot all hold a front-rank berth, meaning Jamie Spencer will likely find her settling further back than ideal; sim-going record of 1 win from 14 is a mild concern on this surface.

runners_data.name: Blue Bolt
runners_data.note: Consistent and in-form at the mile on good ground — four wins from five in similar conditions — and Colin Keane rides a filly who is naturally comfortable racing prominent; the 46-day gap has not blunted her recently, and her form string of 1122-1 signals she rarely runs a bad race.

runners_data.name: Carolina Jetstream
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners a filly whose last two turf runs on good-type going have been limited (2nd from only two comparable starts), and while she is naturally a front-rank type she is one of several such horses unable to get her preferred position in this shape; her strongest form has come on Polytrack and that represents an uncertain profile here.

runners_data.name: Catalina Delcarpio
runners_data.note: William Lee rides a filly who has won at Group level over a mile on good ground, giving her solid credentials on paper, but she is a natural prominent racer displaced by the overcrowded front of this field; her two mile wins came over a slightly longer trip (10f), and stepping back to 8f is worth monitoring.

runners_data.name: Cathedral
runners_data.note: David Egan's mount is a natural prominent racer with a clean record over this course and distance profile — her best form comes when racing in the first half-dozen — and Kevin Philippart De Foy's yard is 0 from 12 over the 14-day window, though the horse's own consistency (placed in most recent starts) is the key positive.

runners_data.name: Dash Of Azure
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's filly has been running consistently over 7f, and this step up to a mile is a question mark; she is a natural prominent type pushed into midfield by the redistribution of traffic ahead of her, which further complicates her task — her single mile run (7th, good ground) does not inspire confidence at this level.

runners_data.name: Falakeyah
runners_data.note: Tom Marquand rides a filly who has won over 10f and 8f on contrasting surfaces — the sim-going record of 1 win from 4 comparable starts is modest — and her tendency to race prominently means she is another displaced by the crowded front rank; Owen Burrows has a 2-from-7 recent strike rate, offering a mild positive on yard form.

runners_data.name: Francophone
runners_data.note: The only confirmed hold-up horse in the field, Christophe Soumillon rides a five-year-old with two wins from 15 comparable-going starts — a low conversion rate — yet her racing style is genuinely distinct from the rest, giving her a structural edge if the pace suits a sweeping late run; 24 days since last run and 10th in her last run at this trip is a caution flag.

runners_data.name: Friendly Soul
runners_data.note: John & Thady Gosden's front-runner carries a STYLE_FIT flag indicating she may not fully hold her natural lead position, yet Oisin Murphy's tactical intelligence makes her the most likely sole pace-setter; her last three wins on good-type surfaces over 8-10f show she can back up her front-running with genuine quality, and controlling the tempo here is her primary weapon.

runners_data.name: Godspeed
runners_data.note: James Doyle rides a filly who was 0 from 8 in comparable going before her recent Listed win, and the step up in class to Group 2 is a genuine test; 55 days since last run is the longest absence in the field, and while she races naturally prominent, her sim-going record of no win from 8 on pure good ground tempers expectations.

runners_data.name: Kon Tiki
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane's mount is a natural prominent racer who wins when allowed to bowl along, with three wins from five recent starts, but the redistribution logic places her at the back of the field — the furthest from her comfort zone of any horse here, reflected in a style-fit score of 0.80; if she can get a clean run from off the pace the form is solid, but this shape does not suit her naturally.

runners_data.name: Noche Clasica
runners_data.note: Kevin Stott rides a four-year-old with three wins from eight starts on comparable going and a strong record at the mile — yet she is a front-rank type shuffled back by the competitive pace picture; Edward Bethell's yard has a modest 14-day window record, and she will need to navigate traffic from a less comfortable position than her form was built from.

runners_data.name: Shes Perfect
runners_data.note: Kieran Shoemark partners a filly who ran just 11 days ago — the freshest horse in the field — and wears a tongue-tie; her form has been placed-heavy (three seconds, one third in recent starts) over 8f on good to soft, and she is one of the few prominent types who could legitimately hold a position in this race without redistribution pressure.

runners_data.name: Snellen
runners_data.note: Gavin Cromwell's five-year-old has the strongest sim-going profile in the field — 15 from 15 comparable runs — and Mark Zahra takes over in the saddle; she is a natural front-rank type who cannot hold that spot in this field and is mapped to midfield, so her best hope is that a strongly-run race allows her to produce a well-timed challenge rather than fight for position from the outset.

races.paceDynamic: Friendly Soul is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with Oisin Murphy aboard, will stride to the front and attempt to control proceedings at a sustainable clip on Good to Firm ground over the straight Ascot mile. The pace will be honest but not frenetic — a single leader dictating without duress creates a genuine test of quality rather than a war of attrition, and horses who can travel prominently behind her without fighting for position will be best placed. This field contains substantially more prominent types than the race shape can accommodate: Snellen, Carolina Jetstream, Catalina Delcarpio, Falakeyah, Arisaig, Dash Of Azure and Noche Clasica are all natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred berth, with Jancis, Blue Bolt, Cathedral and Godspeed the most likely to actually hold front-rank positions behind Friendly Soul. The race shape strongly favours horses that can travel close to a measured gallop and produce a clean turn-of-foot in the final two furlongs — true hold-up specialists are thin on the ground, meaning any late-closing effort will require a large move from an unfavourable position.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Friendly Soul Controls, Quality Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Friendly Soul dictates a steady-to-honest pace unchallenged and the race develops into a quality speed test over the final 2f.
scenarios.body: If Friendly Soul dictates a steady-to-honest pace unchallenged and the race develops into a quality speed test over the final 2f.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pack Quickens Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely honest and a tight cluster of prominent-position horses produce a blanket finish when the tempo increases from the 2f pole.
scenarios.body: If the pace is genuinely honest and a tight cluster of prominent-position horses produce a blanket finish when the tempo increases from the 2f pole.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses, Closers Storm
scenarios.trigger: If the steady pace causes the prominent pack to ease up collectively before the final furlong, allowing Francophone or Kon Tiki to weave through from deeper positions.
scenarios.body: If the steady pace causes the prominent pack to ease up collectively before the final furlong, allowing Francophone or Kon Tiki to weave through from deeper positions.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace War Blows Them Up
scenarios.trigger: If multiple displaced prominent types refuse to settle and force a contested early gallop that burns out the front rank.
scenarios.body: If multiple displaced prominent types refuse to settle and force a contested early gallop that burns out the front rank.

watchPoints.text: Friendly Soul (Oisin Murphy) is the sole confirmed pace-setter — watch whether she is allowed to stride clear or if any of the displaced prominent types, particularly Snellen or Carolina Jetstream, challenge her early and convert a steady race into a contested gallop.

Blue Bolt's draw and early positioning are critical — if Colin Keane can slot her directly onto Friendly Soul's heels in the first furlong, she avoids the traffic created by 13 other horses fighting for prominent ground and travels into an ideal striking position.

Kon Tiki's style-fit score of 0.80 is the lowest in the field — watch whether Billy Loughnane attempts to push forward to reclaim her natural front-rank position or genuinely settles her at the rear, as those are very different races for this filly.

The cluster of seven redistributed prominent types — Arisaig, Carolina Jetstream, Catalina Delcarpio, Dash Of Azure, Falakeyah, Noche Clasica and Snellen — will create a compressed midfield bunch in the early stages; any interference or checked run between the 4f and 2f pole could eliminate multiple fancied runners simultaneously.

Francophone is the only genuine hold-up horse in the race and Christophe Soumillon's ability to find gaps is well-suited to a race where the midfield will be congested — watch whether she is held up wide or finds a clear passage up the rail in the straight, as her route to the line is the most route-dependent of any runner.

races.name: Prince Of Wales's Stakes (Group 1)

runners_data.name: Almaqam
runners_data.note: Five-year-old in excellent form (won last two at 10f on Good), trained by Ed Walker who is 5/29 over the last 14 days — though his natural instinct to press the pace means he is squeezed into a midfield berth here where he will not be at his most comfortable.|

runners_data.name: Dancing Gemini
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse wearing a hood, whose form figures on anything near Good ground are modest (seven runs, one win, two places from 15); stepping up to 1m2f from repeated 8f starts raises a clear stamina question that undercuts confidence even in a scenario that suits closers.|

runners_data.name: Daryz
runners_data.note: Graffard's four-year-old has won three of his last four including back-to-back Group-level wins; he is a natural prominent racer who should secure a clean position just off Ombudsman on this going, and his versatility across 9f–12f marks him as a serious threat.|

runners_data.name: Devil's Advocate
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Gosden, 54 days since last run, whose six outings on Good ground have produced zero wins and zero places — the layoff plus the going record represent genuine concerns even if the pace shape technically offers a route into the race.|

runners_data.name: Mississippi River
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 99 and a horse whose true preference is to race prominently; displaced into midfield by the pace map, he is unlikely to be competitive at this level and his recent form figures (5-1-5-7-0) underline the concern.|

runners_data.name: Ombudsman
runners_data.note: The confirmed pace-setter, OR 128, Buick-ridden for Gosden, who has won four of his last five on Good ground at 9–10f — stepping to 1m2f is a slight query but his control of this race is the defining tactical factor throughout.|

runners_data.name: Minnie Hauk
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners this O'Brien four-year-old who won her last two including a 12f Group success; she is a prominent racer who should find a position just off the pace, and her trainer's 7/31 recent strike rate is solid context for a runner at a major Royal Ascot Group 1.|

runners_data.name: See The Fire
runners_data.note: Balding's five-year-old has won his last two on Good ground at 10f and is in excellent form, but his front-running instincts are thwarted here by Ombudsman's presence; Oisin Murphy will be forced to restrain him into a less natural role, which tempers the appeal of his recent sequence.|

races.paceDynamic: Ombudsman is the confirmed front-runner here and, with William Buick aboard for Gosden, he is expected to dictate at a controlled, honest pace on Good to Firm ground over 1m2f — a trip and surface well within his comfort zone given his recent course-and-distance wins. The field is unusually loaded with prominent-racing types: Almaqam, See The Fire, and Mississippi River are all natural pace-pressing horses who will be squeezed out of their preferred positions by Ombudsman's presence, forcing them to sit deeper than they would choose. Daryz and Minnie Hauk are the most likely to secure the prominent slots directly behind Ombudsman, with both carrying strong recent form and trainers in excellent current touch. This race shape — a single controlled pace-setter, a compressed midfield, and several horses racing against their natural style — strongly favours the confirmed front-runner and the horses who can sit closest to the pace without fighting for it, giving a clear tactical edge to those at the head of affairs or just off it.

watchPoints.text: Ombudsman (Buick/Gosden) dictates this race from the front — if he is never headed before the final furlong he is the horse every other runner must account for, and his control of the tempo is the single most important factor in the outcome.

Almaqam, See The Fire, and Mississippi River are all natural front-runners who cannot all press Ombudsman — watch for early jostling inside the first two furlongs as each jockey attempts to find a forward position, which could compromise their chances significantly.

Daryz (Barzalona/Graffard) has won three of his last four and travels to Ascot in the form of his life — if he settles cleanly just off the pace he represents the most credible threat to the leader in the straight.

Devil's Advocate returns after 54 days off for Gosden, whose yard (7/24 over 14 days) is firing; watch for any market move on the day, though his going form and trip uncertainty make a straightforward win hard to construct.

Dancing Gemini (hood) is racing over 1m2f for the first time having been campaigned exclusively at 8f — if the step up in trip catches him out in the final two furlongs his chance will evaporate quickly regardless of how the pace unfolds.

races.name: Royal Hunt Cup (Heritage Handicap)

runners_data.name: Holloway Boy
runners_data.note: The sole confirmed pacesetter; likely to bowl along uncontested on Good to Firm but is racing here as a prominent type rather than a true front-runner, and the style-fit flag tempers confidence in a front-running win even if conditions suit Burke's consistent six-year-old.

runners_data.name: Skukuza
runners_data.note: Has headgear (visor) and Soumillon takes the ride for Dunlop, but five consecutive out-of-the-frame efforts and patchy form on quick ground make this a significant ask at OR 110 in a 30-runner heritage handicap.

runners_data.name: Linwood
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins for Hannon including at this trip on Good ground, with Spencer booked; 60 days off is the only query but the horse clearly relishes these conditions and is dangerous if the pace sets up for prominent types.

runners_data.name: No Retreat
runners_data.note: Three wins and a second from five starts on Good going makes the going angle compelling; 123 days off is a concern and Loughnane needs to place him prominently, but if fit he could run a bold race from the front end of the field.

runners_data.name: Excellent Believe
runners_data.note: Two wins and two seconds from recent starts suggest solid consistency, though a 7lb claimer (Toby Moore) in a 30-runner Ascot handicap is a significant responsibility; holds a prominent style and likes quick ground.

runners_data.name: Archivist
runners_data.note: McDonald booked is an immediate upgrade; won at 8f on Good last time and the trainer T14 figure of 4/9 is excellent — travels prominently and could exploit a clear run if McDonald positions him astutely in a packed field.

runners_data.name: Cerulean Bay
runners_data.note: Tudhope partners a horse who won at this trip and going but has since run 2nd, 4th in a narrow range — consistent but not a winner found easily; O'Meara's yard firing at a good rate with 10/60 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Ebt's Guard
runners_data.note: Muir & Grassick yard at 0/12 in the 14-day window is a red flag; has placed at 8f on Good ground twice but the form 224-04 shows a recent blank and trainer form does not inspire confidence here.

runners_data.name: Henlein
runners_data.note: Ryan's runner has an unappealing recent string — 7th, 15th, 9th — and while Stott is a competent jockey and the horse has some prior placed form at 8-9f on Good, there is no momentum to speak of.

runners_data.name: Thunder Run
runners_data.note: Interesting that Burke runs this at 1m when all five recent runs have been at 9-12f; stepping back sharply in trip and the form 640-72 is uninspiring, though sim-going record (9/13) shows it handles the surface.

runners_data.name: Chibitty
runners_data.note: 117 days off and a yard that has sent out 0 winners from 7 runners in 14 days; only placed at 10f on Good, and a step back to 8f on fast ground after a long break in a 30-runner field looks difficult.

runners_data.name: Urban Lion
runners_data.note: Won at 8f on Soft last time but has been beaten a long way in multiple outings on Good ground; the sim-going record (1W from 9 runs on similar conditions) is a concern against this quality.

runners_data.name: Jagged Edge
runners_data.note: Keane in the saddle for a horse with three wins at 8f including on Good ground — genuinely prominent by nature but pushed to midfield on the map because the field is loaded with pace; if he gets anywhere near his natural spot, his course-trip profile makes him dangerous.

runners_data.name: Checkandchallenge
runners_data.note: Wears a hood (headgear flagged) and runs for William Knight; a genuine hold-up type but form reads 639-06 and no wins at this level on Good ground — hard to see where the winning move comes from.

runners_data.name: Fifth Column
runners_data.note: Gosden/Buick is always a combination to respect, and the horse won at 8f on Good, but a true prominent type who will be shuffled back by the sheer weight of pace in this field — Buick's skill in traffic may matter more than the horse's natural style here.

runners_data.name: La Botte
runners_data.note: Zahra takes the ride for Eustace on a horse whose form 2-4078 shows no wins and a declining profile; naturally seeks prominent ground but will be denied it in this cavalry charge, and the trainer sends only 1 winner from 10 in 14 days.

runners_data.name: Mister Winston
runners_data.note: Balding yard in excellent form (9/57), Oisin Murphy aboard, and a horse who has won twice at 8f on Good and Soft — a natural front-rank type who may press hard enough to secure a prominent pitch despite a crowded field, and that position would suit him ideally.

runners_data.name: Erzindjan
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore partners a genuine hold-up type who won at 9f on Good last time for TJ Kent; the consistent sim-going record (14/15 runs on similar conditions) and Ryan Moore booking make this one of the more interesting late arrivals.

runners_data.name: One Smack Mac
runners_data.note: 277 days off is a very long layoff for a horse who does like Good ground over shorter trips; the yard has sent out 0 from 14 in 14 days, and returning from nearly nine months off in a 30-runner Ascot handicap is a huge ask.

runners_data.name: Godwinson
runners_data.note: Jack Channon at 1/5 in 14 days is a small yard with limited firepower in this window; form reads 1500-0 and the natural prominent style will be compromised by the weight of pace in this field — hard to see a clear run materialising.

runners_data.name: Ozat
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon partners a horse with a below-par sim-going record (1W from 15 on similar); recent form 248-00 and the yard (0/41 in 14 days) creates a very low platform of confidence.

runners_data.name: Blue Rc
runners_data.note: Hector Crouch takes the ride on a horse who has won at 8f on Standard going and placed twice; wants to race prominently but the redistribution means he will be in a midfield pack rather than his preferred spot — sim-going is 5/11 on grass Good.

runners_data.name: War Socks
runners_data.note: David Egan boards a recent winner (Epsom) at 8f and the horse is consistent in placing at 3-4f Good ground trips; naturally a prominent type who will be squeezed back, but the strong recent form at the right trip makes this a lively outsider if Egan can manufacture a run.

runners_data.name: Shout
runners_data.note: Crisford runners are operating at 3/22 in 14 days and the 3lb claimer Jack Callan takes the ride; form includes a win at 8f on Soft and a 4th at this trip on Good — natural front-rank type shuffled to midfield, which blunts the profile.

runners_data.name: Classic
runners_data.note: Hannon at 9/44 over 14 days is a strong yard stat, and Pat Dobbs rides a horse with two recent wins at 8f on Good ground; a natural prominent type who is capable of holding that position if Dobbs reacts quickly from the gate — one of the better-credentialled of the redistributed horses.

runners_data.name: Swing Vote
runners_data.note: De Sousa takes a long-absent horse (109 days, headgear flag for tongue-tie) with a mediocre sim-going record (3W from 12); six consecutive out-of-frame efforts suggest the rating has overtaken the horse's current level.

runners_data.name: Indalo
runners_data.note: Varian at 2/26 in 14 days is a modest strike rate but the horse has a strong sim-going profile (1W4P from 6 runs on Good at 8f); recently second twice and runs with a hood flag — genuine placed horse but naturally prominent and will be shuffled back by pace.

runners_data.name: Rogue Diplomat
runners_data.note: Consistent placing on Soft going but only 1 win and 2 places from 6 runs on Good; James Owen yard firing (11/47), Harry Davies is a competent rider — but the profile looks softer-ground dependent.

runners_data.name: Scoville
runners_data.note: Haggas and Marquand is a top combination, and a horse who went 2W from 5 on Good ground including a win at 8f; a genuine hold-up type, 68 days off is workable, and if Marquand can get a clear run late, this horse has the class to pick up.

runners_data.name: Witch Hunter
runners_data.note: The form 148900 speaks for itself; a genuine hold-up type but one who has not won at Group/listed level and has multiple poor efforts on similar going — at OR 98 after a prolonged losing run, difficult to see a revival here.

races.paceDynamic: Holloway Boy is the one confirmed front-runner in a 30-runner field, and with Jack Nicholls (5lb claim) aboard on Good to Firm ground at Ascot's straight mile, he is expected to bowl along at a sustainable, uncontested gallop — not a scorching pace, but a genuine, rhythmic one that will stretch the field from the off. Behind him, a mass of natural prominent types — Mister Winston, La Botte, Jagged Edge, War Socks, Classic, Indalo and several others — will be fighting for the handful of positions immediately off the leader, meaning many will be shuffled back into a midfield they do not naturally occupy. The field contains far more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position; of those, Mister Winston (Oisin Murphy, in-form Balding yard, recent winner), Jagged Edge (Colin Keane, three wins at this trip and going), and Classic (Pat Dobbs, Hannon in excellent form) are best-placed by class and jockey to actually secure prominent ground. A honest but uncontested gallop on quick ground at a straight track with a contested early position battle strongly favours horses that can travel prominently without fighting for their spot — true hold-up horses who are genuine closers rather than reluctant passengers will also be well-served as the field fans wide late, but the premium position is just behind the leader for horses whose natural style keeps them there without effort.

runners_data.name: Sand Gazelle
runners_data.note: Buick and Gosden partnership on a filly that has won over 10f on good ground and placed twice at 9f; stepped back in trip to 8f here, and her hold-up style means she needs the pace to be genuine to get into it.

runners_data.name: Muddy Mooy
runners_data.note: Prominent runner for Charlie Pike who showed a second over 10f on soft and a third over 10f at Sandown; drop in trip to 8f looks like a potential concern, trainer has 0 wins from 7 runners in the past 14 days.

runners_data.name: Cheshire Dancer
runners_data.note: Veteran prominent racer who has won twice at 8f on good and carries the hood again for Palmer; has been well beaten on softer ground but 11 of 15 career runs on similar going are encouraging.

runners_data.name: Gaga Girl
runners_data.note: French-trained filly for Gerald Mosse running in the tongue-tie; placed twice at 8f on Heathway and Chantilly, form string shows consistent placed efforts, but switching to Ascot's round mile and a new environment is an unknown.

runners_data.name: American Gal
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's prominent type who has been out of form recently, latest being 9th and 7th in recent starts; 45 days off the track and trainer T14 of 4/36 is moderate — needs a big bounce.

runners_data.name: Betty Clover
runners_data.note: Eve Johnson Houghton filly who ran just 11 days ago; genuinely holds up for her runs and showed a win at 8f on good ground in her history, but recent form of 0-554 is uninspiring heading into a competitive 25-runner heat.

runners_data.name: Radiant Beauty
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on a filly who has won three of her last five including a recent 8f win on good for James Owen; trainer has a strong T14 of 15/58, and she sits comfortably in the prominent bracket at a trip she handles well.

runners_data.name: Rhapsody

runners_data.name: Alobayyah

runners_data.name: Miss Nightfall

runners_data.name: Zgharta

runners_data.name: Seren Star
runners_data.note: William Haggas filly in the tongue-tie who won at 8f on soft and placed over 9f on good; 31 days since last run and prominent style suits a steadily-run race if she can get across from her draw.

runners_data.name: Crystal Flyer
runners_data.note: Hold-up filly for Haslam who has been running over much longer trips of 9-13f; drop to 8f represents a significant shortening and her recent form of 568-97 gives little hope even with the hood on.

runners_data.name: Oolong Poobong
runners_data.note: Edward Bethell's tongue-tie filly who has won at 7f on good and placed twice, including a second at 7f on Newmarket fast ground; her natural game is to race prominently and she may fight for a front berth rather than settle in midfield where she has been mapped.

runners_data.name: Rumba Numba
runners_data.note: Won last time over 8f on good for Varian and Mitchell, just 12 days ago and in excellent form with a 6124-1 string; a genuine prominent type who is one of the most likely to actually hold a handy pitch despite the redistribution tag.

runners_data.name: All Moonshine
runners_data.note: Balding's unbeaten-in-four filly who has won at 7f and 8f, all on Sandown's straight — 126 days off and all her form has come on a very different course configuration to Ascot's round mile, which is an important question mark.

runners_data.name: Perfect Part
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison's hold-up filly placed at 8f on good most recently; form of 0-4642 is modest and only 11 of 15 runs on similar going have placed, suggesting she needs things to fall perfectly.

runners_data.name: Unassuming
runners_data.note: George Boughey's 6-year-old veteran in the tongue-tie who has been running consistently at Sandown; 75 days off the track and five recent starts all on Sandown's straight — transitions to Ascot's very different round mile are historically tricky for such course-specific types.

runners_data.name: Song N Dance
runners_data.note: In-form prominent filly for S Woods and Saffie Osborne with a 211-22 string; has won at 7f and 8f, twice at Newmarket on good, and is one of the horses most likely to actually secure a prominent pitch despite the field compression.

runners_data.name: Callianassa
runners_data.note: Brian Ellison filly who won over 8f on Sandown straight last season; has been off the mark since (form -15576) and 40 days between runs, though the redistribution tag reflects she wants to be forward rather than sitting in midfield.

runners_data.name: Goldilocks Cen
runners_data.note: Lightly raced 3-year-old with only two career runs, both on soft ground — the step up to good-to-firm at Ascot in a 25-runner handicap off 330 days on the track is a very tough ask, and style is unclassified.

runners_data.name: Quamby
runners_data.note: David Simcock's hold-up filly who has placed at 9f and 8f consistently; form of 233-44 shows she is honest but has not won in five starts — needs the pace to be genuine and a clear run from the hold-up position.

runners_data.name: Lady Mariko
runners_data.note: Dylan Cunha's filly who won over 6f on standard and was placed at 7f on soft, but recent runs include an 11th and 6th at 7f on good; wants to race prominently but is one of the horses most likely squeezed out of that position in this congested field.

runners_data.name: Renesmee
runners_data.note: Michael Keady's 6-year-old filly running in the hood, just 12 days after her last run, with form including wins at 7-8f; her natural instinct is to race forward but she arrives with the highest STYLE_FIT discount of any redistributed runner here, meaning her real prospects in an off-pace role are materially dimmer.

races.paceDynamic: Stateira is the lone confirmed front-runner and, with just one natural pace-setter in a 25-runner field, she will dictate terms uncontested from the off, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop around Ascot's round mile on good-to-firm ground. The field is packed with genuine prominent-type fillies — Rumba Numba, Oolong Poobong, All Moonshine, Song N Dance, Callianassa, Lady Mariko, Renesmee, Unassuming, and others — all of whom want to race prominently but physically cannot all occupy that ground, meaning several will be shuffled into unfamiliar midfield positions and compromised accordingly. The most likely horses to actually secure prominent berths behind Stateira are Rumba Numba (in-form, recent 8f winner), Song N Dance (consistent front-rank finisher), and Oolong Poobong (course-proven prominent racer), with the rest forced to cover extra ground. A lone, unhurried front-runner setting an honest but uncontested tempo on fast ground at Ascot's round mile strongly favours horses who can travel smoothly in the first three or four and produce a sustained finish — patient prominent riders and class-on-top types who settle just off the leader will have the clearest run to the line, while true hold-up horses face a stern test of getting through a deep field in time.

watchPoints.text: Stateira (Doyle/Balding) is the sole confirmed front-runner and if she escapes uncontested and sets her own pace, her hold on the race from the front could be very difficult to peg back in a steadily-run mile.

Rumba Numba (Mitchell/Varian) arrives in the best recent form of any horse in the field — a win 12 days ago at 8f on good — and is one of the few redistributed prominent types physically likely to secure a handy position; watch for Mitchell to make sure he gets there early.

The cluster of prominent types (Oolong Poobong, Song N Dance, All Moonshine, Lady Mariko) all wanting to race near the front creates a genuine risk of a scramble for position in the first two furlongs in a 25-runner field — any filly caught flat-footed or forced wide early will be seriously disadvantaged.
Rhapsody (Fallon/Haggas) returns from 248 days off the track — Haggas horses can hit the ground running first time back, but this represents a serious fitness unknown in a race this competitive.

All Moonshine (Watson/Balding) is unbeaten in four but all her wins have come on Sandown's straight mile — Ascot's round mile with a left-hand turn and different rhythm after 126 days off is a very different test, and her form is entirely unexposed on this configuration

races.name: Windsor Castle Stakes (Listed Race)

runners_data.name: A Bear Affair

runners_data.name: Agitator
runners_data.note: Opened his account over this C&D trip on Good, giving this race genuine relevance; he is a natural prominent racer whose preferred ground-level position is under pressure from sheer field size, so his effectiveness depends on threading through earlier than ideal.

runners_data.name: Alfred Wallace
runners_data.note: Won over 7f Good before finishing fifth at this trip, suggesting he may be crying out for further than 6f; bred to be prominent but the field volume means he will be shuffled wider than he'd like, with the drop in trip another query.

runners_data.name: Alpe d'Huez
runners_data.note: Archie Watson juvenile who won over this exact 6f trip on Standard then was placed at Nottingham on Soft, showing versatility; a horse who wants to race handily from the front but will be forced to settle mid-division given the queue of pace types ahead.

runners_data.name: Boleto
runners_data.note: Unbeaten juvenile for Clive Cox, winning his only start at 6f on Good — directly relevant form; wants to be prominent but the numerical overflow of pace horses means Callum Rodriguez must manage a compromised position, dulling the advantage of that one clean piece of evidence.

runners_data.name: Celeron
runners_data.note: Colin Keane rides this O'Callaghan Irish raider who won over 6f Good, the most directly applicable prep; he is among the prominent types squeezed towards the pack but Keane's tactical awareness may allow him to find a better berth than most of the displaced pace horses.

runners_data.name: Charted Course
runners_data.note: Fahey yard form is strong (10/59 in 14 days) and this horse has only one start — a second over 6f Soft; running style unclassified, which makes him one of the genuine wild cards, but the lightly-raced flag means his ceiling and floor are both invisible.

runners_data.name: Dance A Jig
runners_data.note: Beckett juvenile with two seconds at 5f on Good and Soft, now stepping up to 6f and switching from a sprint trip; genuine prominent racer who will be further back than ideal in this field, and the trip extension on quicker ground adds another layer of uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Dorigo
runners_data.note: Single start, placed over 6f Standard, running style unclassified; Kevin Ryan juveniles can spring surprises first time at a big meeting, and the redistribution note suggests he may end up further back than connections plan, which could suit if the pace turns honest.

runners_data.name: Green Sovereign
runners_data.note: Harry Eustace's runner won over 6f Soft and was fifth at Ascot on Standard, giving some course exposure; a natural front-runner by style who, unlike many in this field, is not flagged as redistributed, meaning he has a better chance of finding his berth and racing with confidence.

runners_data.name: Ischgl
runners_data.note: Three runs, all placed, with two seconds at 6f on Good — consistent and directly relevant; a prominent racer who has held his position in competitive fields before and Ciaran Murphy's Irish stable is in decent form, making him one of the more trustworthy pace types in the field.

runners_data.name: King Of Cloughan
runners_data.note: Joseph O'Brien runner placed twice at 7f and 6f on Good, switching back to the shorter trip; classified as unknown in style but has held prominent positions in Irish maidens, and the Good to Firm conditions look fine based on his record.

runners_data.name: One Number
runners_data.note: Another O'Brien juvenile, placed over 6f Good at Navan — form that maps neatly onto today's conditions; Dylan Browne McMonagle is an elite young jockey who can compensate for a less-than-perfect draw, and the prominent style should hold if he gets a clear path early.

runners_data.name: Our Boy Bailey
runners_data.note: Harrington yard sends this runner who was placed over 1m on Good — a significant drop in trip and step up in pace profile; a prominent racer by style but the 8f form base suggests 6f on fast ground may catch him flat-footed in the early exchanges.

runners_data.name: Ruler's Control
runners_data.note: One win over 5f at Heathrow, then a 94-day layoff — freshness can be an asset or a liability; prominent-racing type stepping up in grade after a long break, with no fast-ground experience logged, making him a genuine unknown quantity.

runners_data.name: Sale Shark
runners_data.note: Hugo Palmer's first string, won his only start over 5f Good — strong conditions match; Oisin Murphy booking is significant, and this is one of the few prominent-type runners whose positional aspiration appears achievable given his natural pace and elite pilot.

runners_data.name: Sergei Diaghilev
runners_data.note: Ryan Moore on an A.P. O'Brien winner over 6f Good — as direct a prep as exists for this race; one of the stronger positional cases in the field, and Moore's instinct to slot handily behind a front-runner without expending energy would be ideally suited to the shape Wild Terrain is likely to create.

runners_data.name: Victory Gold
runners_data.note: Suroor runner with a headgear flag (hood) and two runs both on Good at 6f, finishing second and fourth; prominent racer whose form is honest without being dominant, and the hood suggests some freshness or focus issues that could complicate a clean positional run in a 25-horse field.

runners_data.name: Wild Terrain
runners_data.note: The only confirmed pace-setter, wearing blinkers and fresh off a 6f Good win; Hugo Palmer's other runner in the race holds the tactical key for the entire field, and the STYLE_FIT tag means his chance is tempered if the race shape evolves in a way that requires him to do too much too soon.

runners_data.name: Controlla
runners_data.note: De Aguiar yard, second on 6f Good at Newmarket, running style unknown and lightly raced; one of several horses whose profile is essentially opaque beyond a single decent run, and the 31-day gap leaves fitness as an open question in a strong field.

runners_data.name: Freedom Flame
runners_data.note: Won over 6f Good for Richard Hughes, then fourth on Standard — the Good form transfers well here; he is a natural prominent racer whose positional ambitions are squeezed by the volume of similar types, and Hector Crouch will need early decisiveness to avoid being swept back.

runners_data.name: Harlequin Sky
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse placed at 5f Good and 7f Standard, suggesting a middle-distance future; Cieren Fallon rides, and the switch to 6f on sharp ground is not ideal for a type who needs a strong pace to come off, and the pace today looks sustainable rather than truly hot.

runners_data.name: Moonrise
runners_data.note: Balding runner, single win over 6f Standard — form at this trip but on a very different surface; P.J. McDonald takes the ride, and the prominent style gives him a fighting chance if he can slot in naturally, though the jump from all-weather to Good to Firm turf is a real surface switch to factor in.

runners_data.name: On The Queue Tee
runners_data.note: Two placed efforts over 5f Good — a hold-up runner stepping up in trip and in grade simultaneously; Clifford Lee rides for a yard without recent big-meeting form, and the combination of trip extension and hold-up style in a sustainable-pace race makes this a tough ask.

runners_data.name: Troublesome Guest
runners_data.note: Third on debut over 6f Good for Margarson — style unclassified; lightly raced horses from smaller yards occasionally land these big-field Ascot heats but the single run gives minimal evidence to project forward, and J.F. Egan will need fortune in running from whatever draw he receives.

races.paceDynamic: Wild Terrain is the one confirmed front-runner in this 25-runner field and, racing on Good to Firm at Ascot, is likely to bowl along from stall one at a sustainable gallop without being seriously pressured from the outset. The redistribution flags are significant: Agitator, Alfred Wallace, Alpe d'Huez, Boleto, Celeron, Dance A Jig, Freedom Flame and others are all natural prominent racers who cannot all secure their preferred berth in a field this deep, meaning a cluttered early battle for position is probable even if no single rival wants to take Wild Terrain on directly. Those prominent types pushed into midfield will find themselves racing slightly out of role, and the few genuine hold-up runners — A Bear Affair, Harlequin Sky, On The Queue Tee — will be tracking a compressed pack rather than a true gap. The race shape strongly favours horses who can either race handily just behind Wild Terrain without expending energy in the positional scramble, or who possess enough raw speed to cruise through a tiring pack on good-to-firm ground late; true hold-up types are structurally disadvantaged because the pace is sustainable rather than scorching, limiting the late swing.

watchPoints.text: Wild Terrain (blinkers, Hugo Palmer) breaks cleanly — if he gains two lengths in the first 2f uncontested, watch whether any of the prominent pack have the early pace to close that gap before the race effectively settles.

The volume of prominent types attempting to find positions in the first 3f is the single biggest tactical risk; watch for Celeron, Dance A Jig and Freedom Flame in particular being shuffled sideways as the field compresses approaching the 5f pole.

Sergei Diaghilev with Ryan Moore is the standout positional threat — watch whether Moore elects to press Wild Terrain or sit second-off-the-pace, as that decision will set the template for the whole field behind him.

Sale Shark and Green Sovereign both have the natural pace to sit prominent without being redistributed — watch if either secures a clean position inside the first furlong, as that would confirm the pace shape is competitive rather than a Wild Terrain solo run.
